title: SLO metering, silent circuit state, and graceful eviction probe (hotfix)
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: During the incident on 2025-02-12 we observed tenant flapping causing cascades: immediate full-circuit evictions produced traffic churn and KV cache warmup overhead that exacerbated latency SLO violations. This PR introduces a layered mitigations approach: 1) per-tenant SLO metering that maintains a rolling burn-rate score (windowed, decay-based) so decisions use a stability signal rather than instantaneous error spikes; 2) a new "silent" circuit state (probationary) that prevents instantaneous eviction while still deprioritizing traffic and enabling soft-fallback paths; 3) a graceful eviction probe that issues a limited soft-drain attempt with health probe gate and progressive connection handoff before elevating to a full circuit trip; 4) circuit snapshot telemetry that records compact circuit state + recent SLO meter history to S3 for incident replay and post-mortem analysis. The change is deliberately conservative: default thresholds match current behavior (no customer-visible change) and new modes are opt-in via runtime flags and a canary rollout. This PR was cut as a hotfix to quickly land telemetry + probe fixes that were blocking a safe rollback path during the incident. Checklist: [x] implement SLO metering algorithm (exponential decay window + percentile guard); [x] implement silent circuit state and transition rules; [x] implement eviction probe flow with backoff and probe thresholds; [x] record compact circuit snapshots to telemetry with configurable retention; [x] add unit tests for SLO meter and state transitions; [x] add integration tests that exercise probe->evict flow and canary gating; [x] helm values to expose canary flag; [x] changelog and release notes entry. Rollout plan: staged canary (1% qps) -> 5% -> 25% -> full with telemetry verification at each step; emergency kill-switch via feature flag. Rationale: Using a probationary/silent circuit prevents aggressive oscillation and gives the system time to heal while still protecting global SLOs by deprioritizing traffic. Circuit snapshots provide an important safety net for replay and for automated root-cause attribution. Related: ENG-3145 (tenant stabilization), ENG-3251 (post-incident telemetry improvements).

release_notes: New: per-tenant SLO metering and a probationary 'silent' circuit state to reduce oscillations; New: graceful eviction probe to softly drain connections before full circuit trips; New: circuit snapshot telemetry for incident replay and attribution; Ops: helm flag 'features.silentCircuit.enabled' for canary gating; Hotfix: fixes race in circuit manager during probe initiation.
notes_for_qa: How to test locally: 1) enable feature flag in charts/values.yaml; 2) run redwood/tests/test_eviction_probe_integration.py which includes control client that simulates flapping tenant; 3) observe metrics slo_meter.burn_rate and circuit_state tag; 4) validate snapshots are uploaded to test S3 bucket configured via REDWOOD_SNAPSHOT_BUCKET env var. Expected behavior: transient spikes move tenant to 'probationary' state, traffic is deprioritized but not evicted immediately; repeated sustained violations escalate to full 'tripped' state.
